object.description: Lidded neck-amphora attributed to Exekias, the leading Athenian black-figure potter-painter of the mid sixth century BC. On the body a couple ride in a four-horse chariot in a procession, accompanied by a kithara player and a foot soldier, beneath a band of palmettes and lotus on the neck. Exekias' work is marked by precise incision and dignified, static compositions; the lid with its bud-shaped knob survives with the vase. It is a neck-amphora, and the scene is a wedding procession.
facts: Exekias was active in Athens between roughly 545 and 530 BC and worked as both potter and painter.
The vase stands 47 cm high and 24.8 cm in diameter and is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art (Rogers Fund, 1917).
Black-figure decoration is painted in a clay slip that fires black, with details incised through to the red clay.
